**DI60** is a medical diagnosis code designating subarachnoid hemorrhage (*subaraknoidal blødning*). Within the Danish healthcare system, it serves as a critical data point for monitoring the safety and quality of care for patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]]. 

Specifically, DI60 is used in national clinical quality indicators to track the incidence of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|intracranial hemorrhage]] and severe bleeding among patients receiving anticoagulation therapy. By capturing these adverse events, health authorities can evaluate the safety profiles of different treatments—such as Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) compared to Marevan—and adjust clinical guidelines accordingly [^src2] [^src4]. The code is a core component of Indicator 6, which measures the safety of anticoagulation by recording intracranial bleeding events among prevalent atrial fibrillation populations [^src2] [^src3].

To calculate the incidence of intracranial hemorrhage, DI60 is grouped with several other specific codes, including [[di61|DI61]], [[di62|DI62]], [[ds064|DS064]], [[ds065|DS065]], and [[ds066|DS066]] [^src1]. For broader metrics measuring the incidence of severe bleeding, DI60 is part of an extensive list of diagnoses that also includes codes for gastrointestinal bleeding (such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] through [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]) and urinary/respiratory tract bleeding (such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1].

The application of DI60 is consistently documented across the annual 'Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark' reports published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute between 2023 and 2025 [^src1] [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5]. These reports utilize data from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret) to standardize the measurement of clinical indicators, ensuring that complications like subarachnoid hemorrhage are systematically tracked to guide national cardiovascular health policy and regional quality comparisons [^src2] [^src3] [^src5].
